thread:
Incident-Bot: 🚨 Alert: KV-prefill/decode imbalance detected — p99 spike on streaming and generation routes (observed at 11:02 UTC). Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

alex: seeing a big jump in p95/p99 across streaming-api and generate-cntrl. p95 ~ 600ms (baseline ~120ms), p99 ~ 2.3s. Streams show ~12% stalls >1s.

sam: confirmed. Graphs showing sharp rise coincident with large prefill waves from a few heavy customers. Looks like prefill traffic is evicting hot slabs -> increased paging.

priya: is this the kv-slab pressure we saw last month? Any evidence of fragmentation (many small prefills)?

nikhil: heap/kv metrics: slab utilization up to 98% on shard-set A, eviction rate doubled, prefill_count spiked x6 in last 7m. decode latency also increased because decode workers hit page faults.

alex: customer-impact quick check — top 5 customers: 2 have elevated error rates (retries), 3 show slower tail latencies. No 5xxs yet. Notifying support.

pagerduty: @alex — page sent to oncall.

priya: root-cause hypothesis: prefill-vs-decode imbalance. Prefill tasks allocate many KV entries of long contexts, fragmenting slabs and forcing paging for active keys used by decode path. Eviction churn -> streaming tail stalls.

irene: logs show many small prefill entries (avg 3kb) filling slabs that prefer larger objects. LFU eviction is mis-weighted for this pattern.

alex: mitigation options: 1) throttle or rate-limit big prefill jobs (fast). 2) steer prefill to cold pool (requires config flip). 3) temporarily enlarge KV capacity (scale up) — depends on infra. 4) change eviction policy to favor hot-decoded keys (risky). 5) force slab compaction/reshuffle (maintenance).

sam: short-term: enable prefill limiter per-tenant to 0.3x for heavy tenants and reduce concurrent prefill workers from 8 -> 3. Can apply via toggle in control-plane: `prefill.rate_limit.per_tenant` and `prefill.concurrent`.

deploy-bot: @sam — can run config roll. Approve with `deploy config/prefill-limiter v1`

sam: rolling it out to prod canary (10% traffic) in 2m, then 50% in 5m if metrics improve.

alex: while that rolls, can we route streaming traffic away from shard-set A to B/C? Routing policy supports `kv.routing.exclude_shardset`.

nikhil: we have spare capacity on shard-set C but routing change is heavier (needs redispatch warmup). Might cause mini-downtime for affected sessions. Prefer prefill limiter first.

priya: quick probe: reduce `prefill.max_context_size` from 128k -> 32k for canary. That should reduce fragmentation surface area.

irene: also recommend enabling `kv.prefill.dedup_window_ms = 1500` to collapse duplicate prefill attempts for the same key.

alex: customer comms: @priya — please draft a short note for support saying we're investigating increased latency due to cache pressure and working mitigations; ETA 30-45m.

priya: on it. Draft: "We’re seeing elevated latency on streaming and generation. Our engineers are actively mitigating cache pressure caused by background prefetching. We expect improvement within 30-60 minutes. If you're seeing errors, please reply with request IDs"

sam: canary started: applied `prefill.rate_limit.per_tenant=0.3` and `prefill.concurrent=3` on 10% canary. Monitoring.

alex: metrics 2m post-canary: p95 down to 400ms, p99 down to 1.6s, stalls dropped to 7%. Good sign.

nikhil: eviction rate decreased 35% on canary shards, slab fragmentation delta trending down. Prefill allocations per-second dropped ~65% for heavy tenants.

sam: promoting to 50% now.

deploy-bot: rollout 50% complete.

irene: quick safety note: keep an eye on user-perceived correctness. Lowering prefill may increase cold decode work — watch throughput and error budgets.

alex: parallel ops: submitting a maintenance job to run `kv.slab_compact --shardset=A --window=5m` to defragment hot slabs. This is non-disruptive but takes ~10-15m.

nikhil: started slab_compact on A (background). Monitoring IO.

priya: support updated customers. No escalations so far.

sam: 10m update: p95 ~240ms, p99 ~850ms, stalls ~2%. Eviction rate nearly back to baseline. Canary -> 100% rollout approved.

deploy-bot: rollout 100% complete for prefill-limiter.

alex: slab_compact finished. Fragmentation metric improved ~22%.

irene: we saw a few streaming sessions reconnect; those were due to session-level backpressure while routing warmed up. Not related to user content.

priya: follow-ups (action items):
- Add dynamic prefill backpressure: make limiter auto-tighten when slab_util > 85%.
- Revisit eviction policy weights: favor decode-hot keys + longer decay for small-object hotspots.
- Add alert for prefill:decode ratio > 4x per shard.
- Develop on-call runbook for this exact pattern (prefill-driven slab-frag -> paging -> streaming stalls).

nikhil: I’ll make the alert change and sketch eviction weight proposal.

alex: handoff: sam (next oncall) — we’ve mitigated with config limiter rolled to 100%, slab compact applied. Watch p99 and streaming stalls for next 2 hours and be ready to route traffic off shard-set A if we see re-spike.

sam: ack. Monitoring alert thresholds lowered to p99>1s and streaming_stalls>5% for the next 120m.

pagerduty: @sam — you’re oncall.

priya: closing notes: no customer data exposure, no 5xx, impact was elevated latency and reconnects. Postmortem + runbook will be drafted and shared in #postmortems in 48h.

alex: thanks everyone — great triage. :thumbsup:
